title: Marc's Tips for Older Grapplers
excerpt: Brazilian Jiu Jitsu is for everyone — but the way you train in your 40s, 50s, and beyond needs to be a little different than when you were 20. Many older grapplers struggle with injuries, slow recovery, or simply finding
paras: Brazilian Jiu Jitsu is for everyone — but the way you train in your 40s, 50s, and beyond needs to be a little different than when you were 20. Many older grapplers struggle with injuries, slow recovery, or simply finding the right balance between training and life. The good news is that with the right approach, you can keep rolling, improving, and enjoying the art for years to come.

In this video, Dr Marc Barton — BJJ black belt, KJJ head instructor, and former emergency medicine doctor — shares his Top 5 Tips for Older Grapplers . These are practical, battle-tested strategies backed by both science and experience.

Leão, also known by his nickname “Zé Beleza”, is a very close personal friend of Mauricio and Mauricio has arranged this very special visit for us!

Leão is an important figure in jiu-jitsu’s history as he was one of the founding members of the Gracie Barra academy and the Escola de Jiu-Jitsu Leão Teixeira a prime BJJ academy in Rio de Janeiro which is renowned for its work with children. excerpt: Our head instructor, the legendary Mauricio Gomes, is returning for a seminar and grading on December 3rd!
paras: Our head instructor, the legendary Mauricio Gomes, is returning for a seminar and grading on December 3rd!
This is going to be a very special day and will be open to members only. You can book your place here:
Mauricio's biography:
Mauricio began training in Jiu-Jitsu at just four years of age. His father, who was a brown belt, started his journey and took him to classes at João Alberto Barreto’s academy.

As a teenager, Mauricio began training with the legendary Rolls Gracie. Under Rolls’ guidance, he became a highly successful competitor and won the absolute division of the Rio de Janeiro State Championships in 1981. Shortly after this victory Rolls would award Mauricio his black belt. Mauricio continued training with Rolls until his tragic death in 1982.

Through his close ties with the Gracie family, Mauricio met Reila Gracie, the daughter of Carlos Gracie Sr. The two married and, although their relationship didn’t last, they had a son, Roger Gracie. Roger would go on to become a ten-time World Champion and is widely recognised as being the greatest Jiu-Jitsu competitor of all time.

In the late 1990s, Mauricio came to the UK and established the very first Gracie Barra gym there. Through his teaching, many new gyms would open and Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu is now the fastest growing martial art in the UK. Mauricio is affectionately known as the ‘Godfather of British Jiu-Jitsu’ because of his efforts to grow the sport in the country.
Mauricio acts as a mentor to Kingston Jiu Jitsu Head Instructor, Marc, and regularly visits the club to teach classes, seminars and take gradings.

title: Temporary Closure due to COVID-19
excerpt: This has been an enormously difficult decision to make, but we have decided to cancel all classes until further notice. Our students can, however, continue to access classes via our online portal Kingston Jiu Jitsu Onlin
paras: This has been an enormously difficult decision to make, but we have decided to cancel all classes until further notice. Our students can, however, continue to access classes via our online portal Kingston Jiu Jitsu Online and via the Mauricio Gomes Legacy students Facebook group.

Like everyone, we have been watching the events unfold across the world over the last few months, and trying to make decisions regarding the safety and wellbeing of all our club members based on evidence from other countries and experts around the world. Guidance has been confusing for most of us and, with it constantly changing, it has been challenging to know what is the best course of action to take.

Jiu jitsu is undeniably a close contact sport and, while we've tried to keep everyone as safe as possible, we have reached the stage where our health system is already over-burdened and cases of COVID-19 are increasing rapidly.

Jiu jitsu is also very addictive and some will find this decision difficult to understand! But we all have a duty to keep our wider community safe, including the amazing health workers, the elderly and those with complex medical conditions.
All members should have received an email from admin@kingstonjiujitsu.com - if you haven't, please just drop us an email and we'll get back to you.

We feel really lucky to have such an amazing club, and this is really a heartbreaking decision to have made. But everyone is affected by this and we are really grateful for all your support since the club started 8 years ago. And we will come back stronger than ever once it is safe to do so!
Look after yourselves and each other, remember the elderly and vulnerable, stay safe, and look forward to seeing you on the mats again very soon.
